messages:
Maya Lopez: Following up on the ownership pointer RFC: we need an operational playbook for pointer rewrites during compaction and how billing reconciles with previously emitted charges. Short thread to align.
Darren Lee: TL;DR: Don’t mutate the primary ledger. Use indirection for mutable ownership but keep charge events immutable with embedded owner_snapshot. Reconciler emits corrections, not deletions.
Rina Patel: Agree on immutability of charge events. Question: do we store full owner_snapshot in every charge event or a small stable key + snapshot in an archival store? Auditors want cheap point-in-time reconstruction.
Maya Lopez: Ops tradeoff: embedding owner_snapshot in event gives simplest audits at query time but increases storage. We can compress snapshot fields to only {owner_id, owner_type, seq, checksum}. That satisfies auditors while keeping events small.
Darren Lee: Proposal for event envelope fields (compact):
- charge_id
- provenance_id
- emitted_at
- owner_snapshot: "owner:tenant:1234|type:acct|seq:7"
- owner_checksum: "sha256:..."
- enrich_status: {EMITTED, PENDING_ENRICH, CORRECTED}  // as string
ReconcileBot: note: enrich_status must be a string token to avoid schema churn.
Rina Patel: Good. Now pointer table design: pointer key = token_fingerprint, value = current_owner_ref + seq + tombstone_flag + last_updated_ts. Also keep a tiny change-log per fingerprint for history lookups; this is append-only per fingerprint to avoid global transactions.
Darren Lee: How reconciliation works (high level):
1) Reconciler scans append-only charge stream for events with enrich_status != EMITTED or checksum mismatch.
2) For each event, fetch pointer history up to emitted_at and compute canonical owner.
3) If owner != owner_snapshot, emit CORRECTION event referencing original charge_id and include correction_delta.
4) Update materialized billing table (used by dashboards) atomically using idempotent upserts.
Platform PM: We need SLOs for reconcile lag. Business wants invoices stable within 24h, ideally 3h for canary customers.
Maya Lopez: We can adopt a tiered reconcile schedule: canary tenants get near-real-time reconcile (<= 1h), regular tenants 24h window. Reconciler priorities based on tenant flag.
Rina Patel: Edge-case: token fingerprint collisions or reassignments across tenants. We must ensure ownership lease prevents rapid flip-flops. Suggest lease semantics: any reassignment must increment seq and include a min_hold_seconds (e.g., 3600s) unless admin override.
Darren Lee: Also define tombstone behavior: when token is deleted, pointer gets tombstone=true and seq bumps. Charges after tombstone must route to fallback_owner=SYSTEM_RETENTION. Reconciler will mark historical charges per policy.
Maya Lopez: Failure modes on emit path: pointer service down, enrichment timeout, duplicate emission. Emit path rules: always write charge event to ledger with enrich_status=PENDING_ENRICH if enrichment fails. Include emitter_tag so we can trace which service emitted the event.
Rina Patel: For duplicates, rely on charge_id dedupe in downstream consumer. charge_id should be UUIDv7 + emitter_prefix to make idempotency cheap.
Darren Lee: Quick sketch of pointer history compact log entry (stringified to keep event small):
"ph:2026-03-20T12:34:00Z|owner:tenant:1234|seq:8|by:ownership-service"
ReconcileBot: Reminder: keep per-fingerprint logs limited to N entries (e.g., 20) and evict older entries to archive store to avoid hot keys.
Platform PM: Auditability requirement checklist:
- ability to reconstruct owner at any event.emitted_at -> satisfied by embedded owner_snapshot OR pointer history snapshot in archive.
- reconciliation audit trail (reconciler emits correction events referencing original charge_id) -> required.
- checksum verification for fast divergence detection -> required.
Maya Lopez: Operational runbook bullets:
- If reconciler backlog > 6h for canary customers -> page SRE.
- If pointer service 5xx rate > 1% for 10m -> degrade enrich, mark emits as PENDING_ENRICH.
- If audit diffs exceed threshold (0.1% of monthly token volume) -> trigger rollback plan and freeze new pointer rewrites.
Rina Patel: Migration strategy:
1) Phase A: emit owner_snapshot always at event time and use materialized billing table (no pointer table yet).
2) Phase B: deploy pointer service + pointer history (behind flag), reconciler dry-run emit audit diffs to a staging ledger.
3) Phase C: flip reconciler to active corrections for canaries.
4) Phase D: wide rollout once diffs are minimal.
Darren Lee: Security note: pointer table and change log must have strict IAM and audit logging; reconciler actions must be signed to avoid tampering.
Maya Lopez: Next actions: Darren to draft pointer-schema PR, Rina to author reconcile runbook and SLOs, Platform PM to update invoice acceptance criteria, I'll schedule a 30m sync after PRs land.
Platform PM: Thanks—please add the PR links in this thread when ready.
ReconcileBot: reconcilebot: scheduled nightly dry-run at 2026-03-21T04:00Z (results posted to #eng-platform).
Maya Lopez: Thanks team. Keeping this short so we can iterate on the PRs. :white_check_mark:
